_note: News leads (news/leads.mjs). Only feeds meant for automated reading, each fetched live with the pipeline's own honest user agent and allowed by the site's robots.txt on the date in verified_at. primary: the official body's own releases (a news item may be written from them, quotes and numbers checked by code); secondary: press (never published automatically, reported as leads only). A site that blocks automated readers (403, a bot challenge) is listed under rejected and is never worked around. secondary_paths / secondary_titles mark op-eds on an official site: opinion, not an official release, so those items are leads only. sponsor: the member whose own feed it is (a weak match only: it never sets an item's tracker). secondary_paths are tested on both the feed link and the release link ("In the News" press reposts on house.gov are press). state: the two-letter code of a state body's own feed (a bill number with no state written next to it is read as that state's). type html_teasers: an official listing page read like a feed (only teasers with their own machine-readable date).

timing._note: The news step's time limits and windows (news/run.mjs, news/sources/common.mjs). budget_ms: the whole news step (config/publish.json news.time_budget_ms overrides it); leads_budget_ms: the feeds' share of it, at most, and never more than 1/leads_max_part of the total; cadence_slack_ms: a 24 h source read at 06:00 is due again at the 06:00 run the next day; fetch_timeout_ms: one news request (review F2d), also the margin an adapter keeps before its deadline; event_days: no new event older than this; keep_days: links remembered as seen.

structured._note: Structured official-record adapters (news/sources/*.mjs) and news/health.mjs. cadence_hours: how often the source is read and normally has new records; no ok read for 2x cadence is reported stale. max_requests_per_run caps each run (Open States allows about 500 requests/day, 1 per second); min_interval_ms paces requests. jurisdictions: what a source covers ("all", "states" = every jurisdiction but the federal one, or a list). role (state bill sources): aggregator (LegiScan, Open States), legislature_api (a legislature's own API: it confirms the aggregators there and they confirm it, news/confirm.mjs), legislature_site (the legislatures' own hosts, which state bill sources may link to). official_rank: which source is the official record when several give the same event first (news/events.mjs OFFICIAL_ORDER; lower first). run: records true = read from the records the run already has; else order (when the network adapter runs) and budget_share (the most of the news time budget it may use, news/run.mjs).

whitehouse._note: feed itself must answer every run; AI orders are rare

state_legislature._note: Hosts a state bill record may link to (LegiScan state_link, Open States, NY Senate): each legislature's own site, matched exactly or as a subdomain (news/events.mjs hostsFor). legiscan.com is LegiScan's own page, used only when a bill has no state link.

sources._note: NIST news. Most CAISI (now CAISSI) posts are 'updates' this feed leaves out: they come from nist-caissi below.

The CAISI page (https://www.nist.gov/caisi redirects here; renamed Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence) lists its latest posts as teasers with a machine-readable date (news/feeds.mjs parseTeaserPage). Checked live 28 Oct 2026: 8 teasers, incl. the GLM-5.3 and Kimi K3 assessments and the incident-response key practices, none of them in the NIST news feed; robots.txt allows /caissi. NIST's topic feeds for CAISI, CAISSI and super intelligence are valid but empty.
Already a pipeline source: documents become entries and fixed-wording news through the grabber and Tier A / Tier B, so news/leads.mjs does not read it again.

structured_note: Official structured sources for the news rebuild (news/sources/*.mjs, news/CONTRACT.md). hosts: the only hosts an item url may have (https). cadence_hours: how often a run reads it. max_silence_days: health alarm when no item for longer than this (null = silence is normal: the adapter only emits items for tracked entries or AI documents). env: the key variables, first found wins. verified_at: fetched live on that day.
